events.title: Earthquake Shakes Pompeii
events.description: A powerful earthquake struck the Roman city of Pompeii and the surrounding Campania region, causing widespread damage. Repairs were still under way when Vesuvius erupted.
events.significance: The quake is often seen as an early warning of the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 AD, which buried the city.

events.title: Roger Williams Arrives in New England
events.description: The English clergyman Roger Williams arrived in Boston. He later clashed with Puritan leaders over religious freedom and the rights of Native Americans.
events.significance: Williams went on to found Rhode Island, a colony built on the separation of church and state and on religious tolerance.

events.title: The Welcome Stranger Nugget Is Found
events.description: Two prospectors found a huge gold nugget at Moliagul, Victoria, Australia, just below the surface. It is the largest alluvial gold nugget ever recorded.
events.significance: The find became a symbol of the Victorian gold rush, which helped reshape Australia's population and economy.

events.title: United Artists Is Founded
events.description: Charlie Chaplin, Mary Pickford, Douglas Fairbanks and D. W. Griffith launched their own film distribution company. It gave the artists control over their work and its profits.
events.significance: The company challenged the power of the big Hollywood studios and became a model for independent filmmaking.

events.title: Apollo 14 Lands on the Moon
events.description: Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell landed the lunar module Antares in the Fra Mauro highlands. Their mission came after the near-disaster of Apollo 13.
events.significance: The landing restored confidence in the Apollo program. Shepard also famously hit golf balls on the lunar surface.
